rules.title: Contractor's license bond: $25,000
rules.plain_english: Every active license must have a $25,000 contractor's bond (or cashier's check) on file with CSLB to be issued, reinstated, reactivated, renewed, or kept active. An inactive license does not need the bond.
rules.applies_to: All CSLB licensees with an active license (sole owner, partnership, corporation, LLC, joint venture)
rules.source_location: PDF page 295 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt); https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Contractors/Maintain_License/Bond_Information/Bond_Requirements.aspx
rules.verbatim_quote: The board shall require as a condition precedent to the issuance, reinstatement, reactivation, renewal, or continued maintenance of a license, that the applicant or licensee file or have on file a contractor's bond in the sum of twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000).
rules.notes: Subdivision (c): bond not required while license is inactive. The $15,000 pre-2023 amount is from general knowledge of the repealed version (repealed 1/1/2023 per the law book history note) and is not needed for calculations. Bond must be from a surety admitted by the CA Department of Insurance, on an Attorney General-approved form (CSLB Bond Requirements page).

verification.correction: The $15,000 pre-2023 amount is not in the law book text; an official-domain search (leginfo SB 607 / CSLB notice) agrees it was $15,000 before 1/1/2023.

rules.title: Bond: $7,500 cap for claimants other than homeowners/employees
rules.plain_english: Of the $25,000 contractor's bond, the surety's total liability to everyone EXCEPT homeowners who contracted for home improvement on their own residence (B&P 7071.5(a)) is capped at $7,500. The remaining $17,500 is reserved exclusively for those home-improvement homeowners, who may recover up to the full bond. Single-family-home owners, fraud victims, unpaid employees and fringe-benefit trusts share the $7,500.

parameters.priority_beneficiaries: homeowners contracting for home improvement upon the homeowner's personal family residence (7071.5(a))
capped_nonpriority_beneficiaries: single-family dwelling owners not building for sale (7071.5(b))
persons damaged by willful and deliberate violation or fraud (7071.5(c))
fringe-benefit payees, e.g. union trust funds (7071.5(e))

rules.applies_to: Claims against any contractor's license bond
rules.source_location: PDF page 295 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.verbatim_quote: Excluding the claims brought by the beneficiaries specified in subdivision (a) of Section 7071.5, the aggregate liability of a surety on claims brought against a bond required by this section shall not exceed the sum of seven thousand five hundred dollars ($7,500).
rules.notes: 7071.6(b) cross-references "subdivision (a) of Section 7071.5". In 7071.5, subdivision (a) is only home-improvement homeowners. (b)-(e) are separate subdivisions and are not priority. Reserved amount $17,500 derived (25,000 - 7,500).

verification.correction: 7071.6(b) reserves the excess over $7,500 only for beneficiaries in SUBDIVISION (a) of 7071.5, which is just homeowners contracting for home improvement on their own residence. 7071.5(b)-(e) are separate subdivisions (single-family-dwelling owners, willful-violation/fraud victims, unpaid employees, fringe-benefit payees), and they share the $7,500 cap. The extract read the reference as 7071.5(a)-(e) and listed all five groups as priority. Fixed priority_beneficiaries_section, plain_english and notes.

rules.title: Who the contractor's bond protects
rules.plain_english: The license bond pays: homeowners hurt by license-law violations on their own home, owners building a single-family home not for sale, anyone hurt by willful violations or fraud, unpaid employees, and fringe-benefit funds owed employer payments.
rules.applies_to: All contractor's bonds and qualifying individual's bonds
rules.source_location: PDF page 294 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt); PDF page 300 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.verbatim_quote: The contractor's bond shall be for the benefit of the following: (a) A homeowner contracting for home improvement upon the homeowner's personal family residence damaged as a result of a violation of this chapter by the licensee.
rules.notes: Bond must be executed by an admitted surety in favor of the State of California and filed with the registrar. Same beneficiary list applies to the qualifying individual's bond (7071.10).

rules.title: LLC insurance: policy form, insurer and period rules
rules.plain_english: The LLC policy can be claims-made or occurrence, must cover a 'designated period' of no more than 12 months, and must come from a California-admitted insurer or an eligible surplus line insurer. Deductibles/self-insured retentions are allowed.

rules.title: LLC insurance: restore full limit by next policy period or suspension
rules.plain_english: If claims use up the LLC's aggregate limit, it need not buy more for that period, but the full required limit must be back in place by the start of the next designated period or the license is suspended by law.

rules.title: Bond of qualifying individual: $25,000

rules.title: Bond cancellation: license suspended 30 days after CSLB gets notice
rules.plain_english: When a surety cancels your bond, the cancellation takes effect 30 days after CSLB receives the notice. If no reinstatement or replacement bond reaches CSLB in that window, the license is suspended; work while suspended is unlicensed.

rules.notes: CSLB advises arranging a new bond four weeks before the old one expires and matching the new bond's effective date to the old bond's cancellation date. Bond and license renewal dates usually differ.

rules.title: Bond: wage/fringe claims capped at $4,000 total
rules.plain_english: A surety's liability on any one claim for wages and fringe benefits against a license bond (other than a disciplinary bond) is capped at $4,000. If the bond cannot pay all claims in full, claimants share it pro rata. On the $25,000 contractor bond, wage claimants are also inside the $7,500 non-priority pool (B&P 7071.6(b)).

parameters.cap_scope: per claim: the statute caps aggregate liability "on a claim for wages and fringe benefits" (wages plus fringe combined); it is not a ceiling on total wage payouts across all claims

rules.applies_to: Claims against contractor and qualifier bonds

rules.verbatim_quote: The aggregate liability of a surety on a claim for wages and fringe benefits brought against a bond required by this article, other than a bond required by Section 7071.8, shall not exceed the sum of four thousand dollars ($4,000).
rules.notes: "On a claim" (singular) contrasts with 7071.6(b)'s "on claims" aggregate cap, so the $4,000 is per claim. The LLC $100,000 worker bond (7071.6.5) is in the same article. Whether the $4,000 per-claim cap also limits claims on that bond is not addressed. Verify before relying.

Rewrote plain_english and added cap_scope. Wage claimants also fall inside the $7,500 non-priority pool of the $25,000 contractor bond.

Wage and fringe claims must be brought within 6 months of discovering the shortfall and never more than 2 years after the pay was due.

rules.title: FUTA: California credit reduction state (2025: 1.2%; 2026: 1.5%)
rules.plain_english: FUTA is 6.0% on the first $7,000 per employee less a normal 5.4% state credit. California employers lose part of the credit because of the state's federal UI loan: an extra 1.2% for 2025 ($84/employee) and 1.5% listed for 2026 ($105/employee), paid with Form 940 Schedule A.
rules.source_location: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f940sa--dft.pdf; https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/federal-unemployment-tax-act/ (not fetched; search excerpt)
rules.verbatim_quote: California is 0.015 (1.5%).
rules.notes: From search excerpt of the 2026 Schedule A (Form 940) draft; EDD calls 1.5% a projection pending DOL final notice (after Nov 10, 2026). Effective rates and per-employee amounts derived (0.6% + reduction).

verification.checked_against: WebSearch restricted to irs.gov/edd.ca.gov (2026-11-25): the 2026 Form 940 Schedule A draft and EDD FUTA page summaries give California 1.5% for 2026 (labeled projected; final DOL figure after 11/10/2026) and $105 per employee. irs.gov is not reachable.

rules.title: Form 1099-NEC: $2,000 threshold for payments made in 2026
rules.plain_english: For nonemployee compensation paid after December 31, 2025, file Form 1099-NEC for each payee (e.g., unincorporated subcontractor) paid at least $2,000 in the year (was $600). The threshold is inflation-adjusted after 2026. Always file if you backup-withheld, regardless of amount.

rules.title: No 1099 needed for payments to corporations (except attorneys/medical)
rules.plain_english: Payments to corporations (C or S) generally do not require an information return; exceptions include attorneys' fees and medical/health care service corporations.

exceptions: corporations providing medical and health care services or billing for them

rules.title: Backup withholding: 24% if a sub gives no TIN (W-9)
rules.plain_english: If a payee does not furnish a taxpayer identification number (e.g., no W-9), withhold 24% from reportable payments such as nonemployee compensation, deposit it, and report it; for 2026 the backup-withholding reporting threshold matches the $2,000 1099 threshold.

parameters.trigger: payee fails to furnish TIN (Form W-9) or IRS notice of incorrect TIN

rules.title: Sole owners and partners must prepay income tax quarterly
rules.plain_english: If the business is a sole ownership or partnership, owners must prepay estimated federal and state income taxes (quarterly). Federal income tax and Social Security withheld from employees must be paid quarterly, monthly or semimonthly as required.
